Jordan —

Thanks for the note and sorry for the delay getting back to you. Below is our standard approach and the options we can offer given your ask for a 180-day hold. I attached our retention policy and a blank evidence manifest for your intake team.

Summary (short):
- Default retention: hot logs (30 days), cold archive (up to 365 days for audit-ready records) per our SLA.
- Short-term preserved snapshot: we routinely create a preserved copy for forensic review for up to 90 days at no additional charge if requested within 14 days of an incident.
- Extended escrow/retention (beyond 90 days): available as a temporary exception; requires a signed evidence preservation agreement and may incur storage and handling fees.
- Chain-of-custody: we provide a manifest (MD5/SHA256 checksums), transfer receipt, and a timestamped custody log for each artifact.
- Encryption: preserved artifacts are stored encrypted at rest (AES-256). We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for on-request escrow projects, though that requires additional onboarding.

Ask from you: please confirm scope (raw PCAPs vs redacted PCAPs, application traces, or both), approximate total size (GB), and whether Acme prefers Redwood-managed keys or your KMS. Once we have that we can produce a cost estimate and a draft evidence preservation agreement.

Next steps I propose:
1) Jordan confirms artifact list and expected size.
2) Marcus (security) will outline the export and verification steps.
3) We exchange the signed preservation agreement and initiate the hold.

I've attached: redwood-sla-retention-policy.pdf and forensic_evidence_manifest_template.csv.

Best,

Jordan / Vanessa,

Couple of technical clarifications from the security team on how we handle exports and what we can provide:

- Export mechanics: we can produce time-bounded exports from the serving runtime (request traces, server logs) and VM-level captures (where retention snapshot was configured). Raw PCAPs are generated from packet capture appliances and will require a separate forensics pull — provide the exact time window and instance identifiers.
- File formats & integrity: we deliver artifacts in compressed tarballs (.tar.gz) and provide SHA256 checksums and an evidence manifest. We can also provide an MD5 column if your intake requires it.
- Chain-of-custody: Redwood will produce a custody log that records: export operator, UTC timestamp, checksum, storage location, and transfer method. We can notarize the transfer with a date-stamped receipt.
- Encryption & keys: artifacts are AES-256 encrypted at rest. For escrow, we can either: (a) hold using Redwood-managed keys, or (b) encrypt with a customer-provided KMS key (requires KMS onboarding and an HSM-backed key if you need hardware attestation).
- On-prem transfer: if Acme prefers physical transfer (encrypted drive), Redwood supports that under a signed transfer protocol; we will capture chain-of-custody signatures at handoff.
- Cost & SLA: the routine 90-day preservation is within our operational playbook. Anything longer is treated as a temporary SLA exception and is billed as extended escrow storage and handling — typical ballpark is $X per GB/month plus a one-time handling fee. I will ask ops for an exact number once Vanesa confirms scope.

If you want, we can host a 30-minute call to walk the export steps and confirm checksums and the manifest layout.

-Marcus Lin
Head of Security Operations, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

- Data residency: artifacts will remain in Redwood's US region (us-west-2) unless Acme requests export; residency and deletion obligations are captured in the preservation agreement.
